intuition.title: Growth control and surface capping
intuition.text: The authors adapt an earlier two-flask synthesis and vary injection temperature, growth temperature and time to tune the first exciton. Oleic acid is the reported capping ligand. The source does not provide a calibrated process-to-diameter map or a complete ligand-speciation model.

intuition.title: Strong near-infrared fluorescence
intuition.text: The authors interpret the small Stokes shift and high relative quantum yield as evidence of efficient surface passivation and limited trapping. They qualify the quantum-yield calibration because grating efficiency was not corrected; the historical 85% estimate is not a new absolute measurement.

intuition.title: Electronic-transition assignments
intuition.text: An effective-mass model, confinement-energy ratios and intraband spectra jointly motivate the authors’ transition assignments. The unexpectedly allowed second exciton and unresolved expected degeneracy remain open questions in this source. These are model interpretations, not atomistic structural measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–6, Linear absorption, intraband spectra and conclusions

intuition.title: Relaxation without an observed phonon bottleneck
intuition.text: The authors find an unresolved intraband lifetime below 4 ps and discuss acoustic coupling or surface effects as possible explanations. Shape control, core–shell formation and doping are proposed future directions, not products synthesized in this article.

general_background.title: Injection and precursor supply
general_background.summary: Rapid injection can concentrate precursor conversion near the start of a reaction, helping distinguish nucleation from subsequent growth. A short period of rapid precursor conversion can favour nucleation, while a later lower supply can favour growth on existing particles.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Carboxylic-acid and carboxylate ligands
general_background.summary: Carboxylic acids and carboxylates can associate with metal-containing surfaces and solution species through their oxygen groups. The hydrocarbon part of a long-chain ligand can favour dispersion in a compatible solvent, while acid-base equilibria influence how its head group associates.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Prospects of Colloidal Nanocrystals for Electronic and Optoelectronic Applications

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
